answer: Temporal Fingerprint Commitments.** Each identity must publish a signed *sonnet* — a fixed-length behavioral trace of its recent decisions — before acting, and every later action must remain consistent with that trace's hidden hash. A duplicate agent inherits the same trace, so two copies produce divergent continuations that the verifier flags as a fork. To survive, an attacker must maintain distinct, coherent traces across the full *horizon* of each identity's history, paying one full trace-maintenance cycle per clone. A single *quill*-signed deviation collapses the fork.
